US Iran War LIVE | Trump: Permanently Opening Strait of Hormuz | Vantage on Firstpost

Tensions around the Strait of Hormuz are revealing a high-stakes strategic balancing act rather than a total shutdown. While the United States insists it has not closed the waterway, it is effectively strangling Iran’s maritime trade by targeting ships linked to its ports—tracking, intercepting, and forcing them to turn back even far from the Gulf. At the same time, non-Iranian vessels continue to pass legally through the strait, underscoring the fine line Washington is walking to avoid violating international law while still exerting maximum pressure. Iran, meanwhile, is responding with its own calibrated approach—monitoring and selectively influencing traffic from coastal strongholds like Bandar Abbas without triggering a full blockade that could harm global trade and its own interests. The result is a shadow contest where control matters more than closure, and every ship moving through these waters becomes part of a larger geopolitical chessboard.
